name: Discovery Call Prep
summary: Prepares a one-page brief and question plan for a first sales call with a specific prospect.
description: Combines what you know about the prospect with your ICP to produce hypotheses about their pains, questions that test those hypotheses, and qualification criteria to listen for. It never presents guesses about the prospect as facts; anything not supplied is labelled a hypothesis.
problems: I don't know what to ask on a discovery call
My first calls turn into demos too early
I need to qualify leads faster

inputs.label: Prospect
inputs.description: The company and person you're meeting.
inputs.example: Dana Lee, COO at Brightline Agency (35 people)

inputs.label: What you know
inputs.description: Anything you already know: how they found you, what they said, their website.
inputs.example: Booked after reading our post on month-end close; mentioned spreadsheets.

outputs.label: Call brief
outputs.description: Hypotheses, questions mapped to each, qualification criteria and next-step options.

execution.system: You prepare B2B sales reps for a first discovery call. You separate what is known from what is guessed: a fact must quote the prospect information word for word, and everything else, including anything taken from an ideal customer profile, is a hypothesis to test on the call.

prospect_summary.title: Prospect
prospect_summary.description: Who the prospect is, in two or three sentences, using only what was supplied.

evidence.description: The exact words from the prospect or notes that show it, copied word for word.

id.description: A short id such as H1.

statement.description: A guess about their situation or pain.

tests.description: Ids of the hypotheses this question tests.

criterion.description: What would qualify or disqualify them.

listen_for.description: What a qualifying answer sounds like.

next_steps.title: Next-step options
next_steps.description: Options to propose at the end of the call.

steps.name: Prepare brief
steps.responsibility: Draft hypotheses and questions from the prospect notes and ICP.
steps.prompt: Prepare the brief. Only list a fact when you can quote its evidence word for word from the prospect or the notes; otherwise make it a hypothesis. Give each hypothesis an id (H1, H2, ...) and write at least one open question that tests each one, listing the ids it tests. Use the ICP, if provided, for hypotheses and qualification criteria, never for facts. Do not suggest demoing in the first call.

steps.name: Check labels
steps.responsibility: Ensure every stated fact quotes the notes and every hypothesis is tested by a question.

dependencies.reason: The ICP's pains and disqualifiers sharpen the questions.

criteria.description: Claims about the prospect that aren't in the notes are labelled hypotheses: every fact quotes the prospect or notes word for word.
Each hypothesis has at least one question that tests it.
